qt: to the Commission Stanisław Tyszka (ESN) Subject:

NextGenerationEU was financed through borrowing outside the usual expenditure limits of the multiannual financial framework (MFF). However, the debt incurred to finance NextGenerationEU grants will be repaid from future EU budgets over a period ending in 2058, funded by contributions from Member States and other own resources. The fact that grants to beneficiaries are non-repayable does not, therefore, mean that there will be no costs for future EU budgets. In the 2028-2034 MFF proposal, the Commission has earmarked EUR 24 billion per year at current prices for interest payments and principal repayments on the grant component of NextGenerationEU. In view of the above: 1.
According to the Commission’s latest estimates, what will be the total amount of interest and other financing costs for NextGenerationEU up to 2058?
How much will the EU budget spend in total in each year of the 2028-2034 MFF on repaying the principal and interest on the debt used to finance NextGenerationEU grants?

If the proposed new own resources are not adopted, who will foot the bill for the debt used to finance the NextGenerationEU grants: the Member States, through higher contributions, or beneficiaries of other programmes, through cuts to their funding?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.11.2026) The Own Resources Decision provides that NextGenerationEU1 (NGEU) repayments of the principal and the related interest shall be borne by the EU budget, leading to ‘steady and predictable reduction of liabilities’ in accordance with the principle of sound financial management, with no new net borrowing as of 2027, and no outstanding debt after 20582. In line with these conditions, the Commission proposal for the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) 2028-2034 foresees a fixed annual NGEU debt service amount of EUR 24 billion per year in current prices, covering interest and principal for 2028-2034, i.e. EUR 168 billion over seven years. Any amount not needed for interest costs would be used to repay principal. This provides a natural hedge: if interest costs are higher than forecast at the time of adoption of the financial framework, the actual repayment in that year will be lower, and vice versa. A breakdown of total estimated debt service costs can be found in the proposal, without prejudice to future MFF agreements3. 3. The repayment of NGEU from the EU budget is a legal obligation. Under the principle of universality, the total revenue of the EU budget covers all payment appropriations without distinction. No specific own resource can therefore be assigned to the repayment of NGEU. New own resources are essential to support a more ambitious MFF that responds effectively to the EU’s strategic priorities while catering for the repayment of NGEU. Without sufficient new own resources, the budget’s spending capacity could be reduced or national contributions increased.
